newsitem.title: USA: NHL-FOURTEEN DEALS IN DEADLINE FRENZY, LEAFS DEAL MULLER, MURPHY.
newsitem.headline: NHL-FOURTEEN DEALS IN DEADLINE FRENZY, LEAFS DEAL MULLER, MURPHY.

text.p: There were 14 deals closed at Tuesday's National Hockey League trade deadline, with the Toronto Maple Leafs sending away centre Kirk Muller and defenceman Larry Murphy in two of them.

In what is becoming something of a rite of the NHL trading dealine, Muller was dealt again. This time the former captain of the New Jersey Devils and Montreal Canadiens was sent to the Florida Panthers for rookie forward Jason Podollan.

The rebuilding Leafs also sold defenceman Larry Murphy and his lucrative contract to the Detroit Red Wings, who did not have to part with any manpower to get the league's third highest-scoring defenceman ever.

Muller was Devils' captain before he was traded to Montreal before the 1991-92 season for Stephane Richer. He shared the coveted Montreal captaincy with Guy Carbonneau and led the Canadiens to the Stanley Cup in 1992-93.

Muller was traded to the New York Islanders in April 1995, but left them because he did not want to play for a rebuilding team and eventually was shipped off to Toronto in a three-way deal involving the Ottawa Senators.

In 66 games for the Maple Leafs this season, the 31-year-old Muller has 20 goals -- nine on the power play -- and 17 assists but is minus-22. In 952 games, Muller has 325 goals and 519 assists for 844 points.
The 21-year-old Podollan had a goal and an assist in 19 games for the Panthers this season.
Murphy has registered seven goals and 32 assists in 69 games and has managed to compile a plus-2 rating on one of the league's worst teams.
In 1,303 career game, Murphy has 252 goals, 793 assists and 1,045 points, trailing only Paul Coffey and Raymond Bourque among defenceman on the all-time scoring list.

In other deadline deals, the Los Angeles Kings sent veteran centre Eddie Olczyk to the Pittsburgh Penguins for big right winger Glen Murray, 24, who has yet to live up to expectations in 283 NHL games with Boston and Pittsburgh.
The Pens also picked up right wing Roman Oksiuta from the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim for Korean-born centre Richard Park.
The Islanders traded left wing Derek King, who had been with the team since 1986, to the Hartford Whalers for a 1997 fifth-round draft pick.
Hartford also sent tough guy Kelly Chase to Toronto for a 1998 eighth-rounder and dealt centre Mark Janssens to Anaheim for left wing Bates Battaglia and a 1998 fourth-round pick.

Another deal occurred between the Phoenix Coyotes and the Canadiens. The Coyotes, who have started goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin in 31 straight games, acquired 29-year-old backup Pat Jablonski for 21-year-old defenceman Steve Cheredaryk.
Olczyk, who signed with the Kings as a free agent in July, has 21 goals and 23 assists in 67 games. The 31-year-old centre has 315 goals and 419 assists in 869 career games.
Murray, Boston's first-round draft choice in 1991, has 11 goals and 11 assists in 66 games this season and 54 goals and 56 assists in his career.
The 26-year-old Oksiuta has struggled through an injury-plagued season with six goals and seven assists in 28 games but adds size to the Penguins.
Park, 20, played his only game this season for Pittsburgh last week. He spent the rest of the year with Cleveland of the International Hockey League, notching 12 goals and 15 assists.
King had been with the Islanders longer than any other current player. The 30-year-old forward was second on the team in scoring with 23 goals and 30 assists in 70 games.
The Isles stand to gain from Toronto's trades of Muller and Murphy. New York owns the Leafs' pick in the June draft, which could become the top overall selection if Toronto finishes last in the NHL.

Montreal and Phoenix traded again before the deadline, with the Canadiens acquiring hard-hitting defenceman Dave Manson for defenceman Murray Baron and right wing Chris Murray. The Coyotes turned around and sent Murray to Hartford for rugged defenceman Gerald Diduck.
The Edmonton Oilers were also busy, sending defenceman Jeff Norton to the Tampa Bay Lightning for young defenceman Drew Bannister and a sixth-round draft choice in 1997.

The Oilers swung another deal, sending 22-year-old left wing Miroslav Satan to the Buffalo Sabres for left wing Barrie Moore and defenceman Craig Millar. Satan had 17 goals and 11 assists in 64 games.
